task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: cut-heavy role (high initiation share of CUT play type)
drive-heavy role (high initiation share of DRIVE play type)
role portability (stability of player's initiation profile or structural influence across teams)
methodological_questions: How to define and measure a cut-heavy vs. drive-heavy shaper using play-type initiation shares?
Operationalising 'role travels better': play-type profile similarity, structural influence change, or displacement persistence after a move?
Identifying off-season shaper movers across multiple seasons with reliable sample sizes
Separating true role portability from confounding by team system, usage change, position, and player age
evidence_establishes: No prior project evidence is available for the specific comparison of cut-heavy vs. drive-heavy shapers.
evidence_does_not_establish: No evidence on whether cut-heavy shapers have more stable roles when changing teams.
No baseline on typical structural influence transfer for shapers.
No established measure of role portability from earlier work.
own_inferences: Cut-heavy shapers may depend more on off-ball movement and system-independent timing, while drive-heavy shapers need on-ball opportunities and specific spacing; this could make cut-heavy roles more portable.
Play-type initiation shares can serve as a direct behavioural fingerprint of a player's role, and cosine similarity (or Euclidean distance) is a natural measure of role preservation.
The available data span four off-seasons (2023–2026), likely providing enough shaper movers to make the question testable with n = 24 units (the recorded sample), though power may be limited.
A within-player design comparing profile similarity across moves avoids many between-player confounds but is still subject to changes in team context and usage.
uncertainties: The exact meaning of n = 24 (whether players, player-moves, or teams) is not stated, affecting power calculations.
Reliability of CUT and DRIVE classifications from the inferrer may blur the distinction between cut-heavy and drive-heavy.
Sampling of shapers who move is non-random and may be confounded with age, contract type, or team rebuilding status.
There is no prior evidence on the variance of role-portability measures for shapers, so a formal power analysis is impossible.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval returned no prior studies, so the decision is based entirely on the research question and the available data.

blocking_constraints.text: Only n=24 units are available, and if these are mover-seasons, the effective sample for a two-group comparison will be small (≈12 per group), severely limiting power.
Shaper-identified players who also change teams in a given off-season and have enough recorded initiations of both CUT and DRIVE may be rare, leading to very small cell sizes.
Play-type classification (especially CUT vs. DRIVE) can be noisy, and small differences in shares may lead to misclassification of cut-heavy vs. drive-heavy, diluting effects.
Changes in role similarity may be driven by factors like change in team offensive system, player usage change, position, and age, not by inherent portability of cut vs. drive roles.

prior_work.summary: No earlier studies from the project were retrieved. The Structural Influence paper defined Shaper as a role category, but did not compare cut-heavy vs drive-heavy sub-types.

risks.text: The recorded n=24 leaves little room for robust inference after splitting by play-type emphasis; effect sizes would need to be very large to be detectable.
Few shapers are likely to be extreme cut-heavy or drive-heavy with a clean off-season move, risking empty cells when applying minimum initiation thresholds.
Misclassification of play types (CUT vs DRIVE) could bias the grouping variable toward the null, reducing power.
Differences in role portability may be attributed to cut vs. drive style but actually be driven by correlated player characteristics (e.g., size, position, athleticism, or team decision to trade).
The base rate of shapers who move off-season may be low; even if 24 mover observations exist, they may not split evenly into the two style groups.

design.estimand: Difference in role portability between cut-heavy and drive-heavy Shaper movers, where role portability is the cosine similarity between a player's normalized play-type initiation vector (shares of CUT, DRIVE, SPOT_UP, PNR_BALL_HANDLER, POST_UP, PUTBACK, TRANSITION, and PULL_UP) measured in their last full season with the old team and their first full season with the new team.
design.unit: Off-season team move by a Shaper player.
design.sample: All players classified as Shapers (low usage, positive residual structural influence) in any regular season from 2022-23 through 2024-25, who (a) changed teams during the following off-season (trade or free-agency signing), (b) played at least 40 games and initiated ≥200 possessions in both the pre-move and post-move regular seasons, and (c) had a clear majority of CUT or DRIVE initiations relative to each other: cut-heavy if share_CUT > share_DRIVE, drive-heavy if share_DRIVE > share_CUT (ties excluded). Mid-season trades are excluded; only off-season moves are used to give time for role assimilation.
design.power: Formal power calculation is not possible without pilot data. The full design uses all eligible movers across the available seasons; assuming n≈24 eligible mover-seasons and a plausible large effect (Cohen's d ≈ 1.0), a two-sided two-sample t-test at α = 0.05 would have approximately 0.50–0.60 power. The study is therefore best viewed as an exploratory estimate with uncertainty intervals rather than a strict hypothesis test.
design.controls: Because the design is within-player (pre vs. post), many stable player traits cancel out. To address remaining confounding, we will control for: change in overall usage rate from pre- to post-move, absolute change in team pace, player age, and a binary indicator of position (guard/wing vs. big). The primary analysis will use a linear regression of cosine similarity on group (cut-heavy = 1) plus these covariates; a secondary unadjusted Welch t-test robustness check will be reported.
design.falsification: 1) Shuffle test: randomly permute the cut/drive label among movers to check that any apparent difference is not a chance property of the similarity distribution. 2) Placebo non-movers: apply the same classification to Shapers who did not move, measuring ‘pseudo-similarity’ between consecutive seasons; the cut/drive difference should be absent or smaller in non-movers if the mover effect reflects role portability. 3) Sensitivity to play-type misclassification: repeat analysis after dropping possessions where inferrer confidence is below a threshold.
design.multiplicity: The primary hypothesis is a single comparison (cut-heavy vs. drive-heavy on cosine similarity). Correction for the multiple play types used in the vector is not needed because the similarity measure aggregates them. We will not test other portability measures unless the primary is null, in which case we will label any secondary test as exploratory.
design.decision_rule: The study will estimate the difference in mean cosine similarity (cut-heavy minus drive-heavy) with a 90% confidence interval. A pre-specified region of practical equivalence (ROPE) will be set at [−0.1, 0.1]. If the 90% CI lies entirely above the ROPE, we conclude cut-heavy roles travel better; if entirely below, drive-heavy travel better; otherwise the result is inconclusive. Null-hypothesis testing is secondary to estimation.
design.data_version: Per-game and possession-level data from NBA 2022-23 through 2025-26 seasons as available on 2026-08-08, using the project’s standard play-type classifier and structural influence pipeline (2025 release).
